title: Commission Notice on the application of the sustainable finance framework and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive to the defence sector (OJ C/2025/4950)
date_evidence: The Commission Notice on the application of the sustainable finance framework and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD) to the defence sector was published in the Official Journal of the EU on 30 December 2025.
key_claim: EU sustainable finance framework is compatible with defence investing; defence may qualify as a sustainable investment under SFDR via contribution to UN SDG 16 (peace, justice, strong institutions); generalised defence exclusions are 'inconsistent with the EU's strategic needs and priorities'.
notes: Structural anchor: 30 December 2025 OJ publication is the binding regulatory pivot beneath the ReArm Europe narrative; cited inline like any other source.

title: EIB Group powers up flagship investment instruments to boost Europe's tech leadership and defence capabilities
date_evidence: EIB Group powers up flagship investment instruments to boost Europe's tech leadership and defence capabilities ... 25 March 2026 ... Reference 2026-113-EN
key_claim: EIB Boards endorsed expansion of the Defence Equity Facility from initial €175 million envelope to an initial target size of €1 billion fund-of-funds, projected to support up to 20 new defence and cybersecurity funds; ETCI platform launching Q2 2026 targets €15 billion in pledges to mobilise €80 billion in investments including defence.
notes: Tier 1 EU institution press release. Quantification anchor for fund-of-funds scaling.

publisher: European Commission, DG Defence Industry and Space
title: SAFE approvals unlock defence funding for Czechia and France
date_evidence: News article  26 March 2026  Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space ... Publication date :   26 March 2026
key_claim: Czechia and France entitled to €2.06 billion and €15.09 billion respectively under SAFE; Council had already adopted implementing decisions for 16 Member States by 26 March; first SAFE payments expected April 2026.
notes: Tier 1 quantification anchor for SAFE deployment scale.

publisher: European Commission, DG Defence Industry and Space
title: InvestEU Defence Equity Facility: the European Investment Fund commits €50 million to Join Capital Fund III for European deeptech and dual-use
date_evidence: News article  4 March 2026  Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space ... Publication date :   4 March 2026
key_claim: EIF commits €50 million (its largest defence commitment to date) to Join Capital Fund III via InvestEU Defence Equity Facility; Fund III targets €235 million across 25 early-stage deeptech, dual-use, security and space startups; EIF credibility 'acts as a seal of approval signalling to other investors'.
verbatim_quote: This investment is not only funding. The EIF credibility also acts as a seal of approval signalling to other investors the relevance of the aerospace and security and defence sector.
notes: Tier 1 EU institution press release; the EIF quote is verbatim from page.

title: EU Defence Readiness Omnibus: security, industry, and ESG intersections
key_claim: Defence 'once largely excluded from ESG frameworks' is being repositioned as a contributor to resilience and social sustainability; EIB now permits up to €3 billion in defence-related loans including €1 billion for dual-use infrastructure; Omnibus targets unlocking €800 billion in defence investment over four years, with €42-51 billion in cumulative benefits expected over the next decade.
verbatim_quote: Defense, once largely excluded from ESG frameworks, is now becoming a part of these, marking a move to a more risk-based and pragmatic approach
notes: Tier 2 institutional research from major law firm; useful for the omnibus framing and the €3bn EIB number.

title: Norway Wealth Fund Says Weapons Exclusions Are Hurting Returns
date_evidence: Norway Wealth Fund Says AI Caught Risks That Others Missed - Bloomberg https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-02-26/norway-wealth-fund-says-weapons-exclusions-are-hurting-returns
key_claim: Norway's GPFG, the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, publicly states that weapons exclusions are hurting returns; a parliamentary review (committee report due 15 October 2026) could open up to ~$1 trillion in defence-company market cap including Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Airbus, BAE Systems, Safran, Thales, Northrop Grumman.
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism; paywalled but URL-date and search snippet confirm 26 February 2026 publication; primary source for the GPFG return-pressure data point.

title: Germany's Sovereign Wealth Fund Is Dropping Weapons Exclusions
date_evidence: Germany's Sovereign Wealth Fund Is Dropping Weapons Exclusions https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-20/germany-s-sovereign-wealth-fund-is-dropping-weapons-exclusions
key_claim: Kenfo, Germany's €24bn nuclear-waste fund and one of its sovereign wealth pools, abandons its 5% defence-revenue exclusion ceiling, permitting equity and bond holdings in conventional-weapons companies headquartered in the EU, UK, Norway or Switzerland.
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism; paywalled URL but date is in the URL slug and confirmed across multiple secondary reports (Pravda Germany, Voice of Emirates, Irish Times all dated 20-21 April 2026).

title: Defence and sustainable investment debates need more nuance, says Eurosif
date_evidence: news article published 17 hours ago, based on May 27, 2026 ... Eurosif has published a discussion paper providing 'a comprehensive overview of the interaction between sustainable investment and the defence sector'
key_claim: Eurosif executive director Aleksandra Palinska says 'investor approaches across Europe remain diverse, reflecting different cultural, geographical, and historical contexts'; a 2026 Jefferies survey found 28% of investors reviewing their defence policies (down from 38% in 2025) and 23% had changed policies to become more favourable to defence — indicating the market may be moving from policy reassessment to implementation; some sustainable funds are still excluding the sector completely.
verbatim_quote: investor approaches across Europe remain diverse, reflecting different cultural, geographical, and historical contexts, varying client preferences, and differing interpretations of sustainability
notes: Counter-argument source: Eurosif (Europe's umbrella body for sustainable investment) cautions against a one-way narrative; Jefferies-survey data point anchors the counter-counter.
